title: Separable normalization residue fields after the group-order root extension
statement: Let i:U -> L and W -> U be a finite etale G-torsor, G finite. Let phi:Spec R -> L, f in R, and an isomorphism beta:U times_L Spec R = D(f) compatible with the maps to Spec R. Let H be a commutative Noetherian R-algebra via b, put g=b(f) and n=|G|, assume n is invertible in H, multiplication by g is injective, and H/(g) is a domain. Set A=H[t]/(t^n-g), N=Spec A and V=D(g). Assume prime localizations containing t are regular local and N is locally Noetherian. Pull the given torsor back to $V$, obtaining $p:P\to V$. Assume $p$ is finite etale. Set $a=p\circ V.\iota:P\to N$ and let $a^{\mathrm{norm}}:a.\mathrm{normalization}\to N$ be its concrete relative normalization; assume this map is finite. Let j:D -> N be a regular integral effective Cartier centre with image N minus V. At each normalization point $x$ above $j(\eta)$, where $\eta$ is generic in $D$, the field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(a^{\mathrm{norm}}(x))$ induced by the canonical residue-field map is separable: every element satisfies a separable polynomial over the base field. No maximal-ideal equality is included.

source.place: Tags 09EB (more-algebra-lemma-galois-conclusion), 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), 0EYG (pione-lemma-abhyankar-one-divisor), and 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); the residue-separability clause. Tag 09E7 (adic formal smoothness criterion) identifies the two conclusions of adic formal smoothness.

proof.text: Obtain divisibility of the canonical normalization residue-field degree by |G| without using invertibility.

Map the unit |G| from H into the base residue field via the coefficient map and canonical spectrum evaluation. Since |G|>0, the degree divisibility forces finite dimensionality. Its inseparable degree divides its total degree and is a power of the exponential characteristic. In characteristic zero this power is one. In prime characteristic a positive exponent would make the characteristic divide |G|, contradicting the mapped unit. Thus the inseparable degree is one, giving separability by Mathlib.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09EB; the Galois residue-degree step followed by the prime-power inseparable-degree argument, formalized using Mathlib.FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Basic

theorem root_normalization_generic_stalk_residue_separable
    {L U : Scheme.{u}} (i : U ⟶ L)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (W : GaloisCover G U)
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : Spec R ⟶ L) (f : R)
    (β : pullback i φ ≅ Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec R)
      (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))
    (hβ : β.hom ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec R)
      (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) = pullback.snd i φ)
    (H : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsNoetherianRing H] (b : R ⟶ H)
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : H)) (hg : IsSMulRegular H (b.hom f))
    [IsDomain (H ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f})] :
    let g := b.hom f
    let A := AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial H) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C g)
    let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
    let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap H A))
    let V : N.Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H A g)
    (∀ (Q : Ideal A) (hQ : Q.IsPrime),
      letI := hQ
      AdjoinRoot.root ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial H) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C g) ∈ Q →
        IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime Q)) →
    ∀ (hN : IsLocallyNoetherian N),
    letI := hN
    let p := pullback.snd (W.π ≫ i) (V.ι ≫ q ≫ Spec.map b ≫ φ)
    ∀ (hp : IsFinite p),
    letI := hp
    let a := p ≫ V.ι
    Etale p → IsFinite a.fromNormalization →
    ∀ (D : Scheme.{u}) (j : D ⟶ N),
      IsRegular D → IsIntegral D → IsEffectiveCartierCenter j →
      (∀ z : N, z ∈ V ↔ z ∉ Set.range j) →
      ∀ (η : D), IsGenericPoint η Set.univ →
      ∀ (x : a.normalization), a.fromNormalization x = j η →
        letI := (a.fromNormalization.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsSeparable (N.residueField (a.fromNormalization x))
          (a.normalization.residueField x)
